title: Did the NYC Care Program Reduced the Uninsured Rate in NYC? Evidence from a Comparison Study of Puerto Ricans, Mexicans and the White Non-Hispanic
content: In January 2019, the city of New York launched the New York City Care (NYC Care) program aiming to reduce the uninsured rate for individuals facing income and wealth constraints, or with undocumented status. Using a sample of American White non-Hispanic, Puerto Rican and Mexican individuals born between 1963 and 1994 from the 5-year American Community Survey for the years 2018, 2019 and 2022 the study employs a Bivariate Probit Model to identify the effect of the NYC Care program. Results show that the program increased the probability of having public insurance in the year 2022. When the model interacts the effects of the NYC Care program with the ethnicity, results show that the observed effect is mainly explained by the increase in public insurance among the Mexico born population of New York City. Despite the above result, the descriptive statistics demonstrate that the rate of uninsurance among that population remains well below the uninsurance rate observed among the White non-Hispanic and Puerto Ricans.
